week_log.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
facts: OpenAI proposes perplexity (cross-entropy loss) as a shared industry metric for AI progress and safety.
Jakub Pachocki argues that training better compressors is key to understanding AI capability advancement.
OpenAI published internal perplexity measurements to encourage industry-wide transparency.
Perplexity measures the average next-token prediction accuracy of a model.
Current OpenAI models have reached log-perplexity levels below 0.8.
Pachocki suggests establishing common development limits based on perplexity milestones.
AI is increasingly contributing to its own pretraining and algorithmic research.
Future transformative capabilities are expected as models reach the 0.68-0.7 log-perplexity window.

week_log.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Release 2026/09/10
facts: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash released with native visual understanding.
Features a 552B-parameter MoE with asymmetric architecture.
Uses 8B active parameters for input and 16B for output.
KV cache requirements reduced to 1/4 HBM and 1/8 SSD storage.
Outperforms DeepSeek-V4-Pro in benchmarks, speed, and cost.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro requests to route to V4.1-Flash starting Sept 14, 2026.
New pricing structure with off-peak rates at 50% of peak.
Model weights and technical report available on Hugging Face.

facts: DeepSeek-V4-Pro is now generally available.
DeepSeek API now supports web search, file input, and URL reading.

week_log.title: DeepSeek-V4 Preview Release 2026/04/24
facts: DeepSeek-V4 released with Pro and Flash variants
DeepSeek-V4-Pro features 1.6T total and 49B active parameters
DeepSeek-V4-Flash features 284B total and 13B active parameters
Both models support 1M context length

DeepSeek-chat and deepseek-reasoner to be retired July 24th, 2026
Models feature integrated thinking and non-thinking modes

tweets: Qwen3.8-27B is out on Hugging Face. It's a 27B dense vision-language model supporting images and hour-scale videos, with native 262k context extensible to 1M. Compatible with HF Transformers, vLLM, and SGLang. Hosted API on Qwen Cloud is coming soon.

Qwen dropped Qwen3.8-27B. It brings big gains in coding, agentic tasks, and visual reasoning into a compact 27B model. Thinking mode is on by default but adjustable. You can grab the weights on Hugging Face now, with a managed Qwen Cloud API coming soon.
342573727.source: Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B  Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B · Hugging Face Qwen3.8-27B This repository contains model weights and configuration files for the post-trained model in the Hugging Face Transformers format. These artifacts are compatible with Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, SGLang, TokenSpeed, etc. For users seeking managed, scalable inference without infrastructure maintenance, the official Qwen API service is provided by Qwen Cloud . In particular, Qwen3.8-27B will be available as a hosted version with more production features, e.g., 1M context length by default, official built-in tools. For more information, please refer to the Qwen3.8-27B Overview . The service is coming soon. Stay tuned for updates. Following the widespread community adoption of the Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6 series, we are pleased to introduce Qwen3.8, the most capable generation in the Qwen open-model family to date. Built on the architectural foundation of Qwen3.5, Qwen3.8 delivers substantial gains across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. Qwen3.8-27B brings these advances to a compact, deployment-friendly dense model: a native vision-language model that understands images and videos, with flexible thinking control, designed to carry complex, multi-step tasks through to completion with greater reliability. Qwen3.8 Highlights Qwen3.8-27B features the following enhancements: Core Capabilities : Comprehensive improvements across coding, professional work, research, and long-horizon agentic tasks. Agent Execution : Stronger autonomous planning and better handling of environment feedback, leading to more reliable end-to-end task completion. Downstream Compatibility : Broader support for popular harnesses and development tools, making it easier to integrate into your existing stack. Flexible Thinking Control : Thinking mode is on by default and can be disabled per request; reasoning depth can be tuned with reasoning_effort , and reasoning context from historical messages is retained via preserve_thinking . Vision-Language Understanding : Native support for image and video understanding, from STEM diagrams and documents to hour-scale videos. Model Overview Type: Causal Language Model with Vision Encoder Training Stage: Pre-training & Post-training Language Model Number of Parameters: 27B Hidden Dimension: 5120 Token Embedding: 248,320 (Padded) Number of Layers: 64 Hidden Layout: 16 × (3 × (Gated DeltaNet → FFN) → 1 × (Gated Attention → FFN)) Gated DeltaNet: Number of Linear Attention Heads: 48 for V and 16 for QK Head Dimension: 128 Gated Attention: Number of Attention Heads: 24 for Q and 4 for KV Head Dimension: 256 Rotary Position Embedding Dimension: 64 Feed Forward Network: Intermediate Dimension: 17,408 LM Output: 248,320 (Padded) MTP (Multi-Token Prediction): trained with multiple steps Context Length: 262,144 natively and extensible up to 1,000,000 tokens. Ask the assistant to inspect your scene, create a product-display layout, arrange objects, assign materials or prepare an export. Keep working in Blender throughout the process. mcp-for-blender-pro brings conversation, scene tools, model choice and agent workflows together. Workers: perform the assigned scene operations. Reviewers: inspect results and approve work or return specific findings. Tasks run sequentially so scene edits stay ordered. tweets: OpenRouter addressed security findings showing some inference providers breached data policies. OpenRouter itself wasn't breached, but they off-boarded 3 providers, removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention eligibility, and notified all affected users.

Security researchers found data policy issues with several AI inference providers. OpenRouter wasn't breached, but they've off-boarded 3 providers and stripped 125 endpoints of Zero Data Retention status while directly notifying impacted customers.
342593125.source: Data Processing Incidents on Inference Providers  Data Processing Incidents on Inference Providers Data Processing Incidents on Inference Providers OpenRouter · 11/22/2026 Provider security announcements Provider security announcements Earlier this week, security researchers reported that certain inference providers had data compromised or otherwise shown evidence that their data policies were not being upheld. We have been collaborating closely with the researchers and with providers to understand the findings and encourage the providers to address them. These findings did not show any breach or unauthorized access of OpenRouter. The results of this testing revealed new findings about specific inference providers. A live list of the security announcements we have received from providers is below . As the operating layer between customers and a fast-moving ecosystem of models and providers, we take data policy enforcement very seriously. We have taken the following actions: Off-boarded three providers from OpenRouter, based on the results of our investigations. Removed 125 endpoints from Zero Data Retention (ZDR) eligibility. The removals included providers flagged by researchers, plus additional endpoints that we removed as a precautionary measure. Notified all potentially affected customers. The following work is underway: We are adapting the researchers’ testing approach so we can run these checks on an ongoing basis. We are conducting technical verification of network paths to identify instances where requests and responses may be being forwarded to third parties. We are requiring appropriate assurances and validation before restoring ZDR eligibility to any endpoint removed in this review. We are grateful for the Dragos report. As we integrate similar testing techniques into OpenRouter, we will keep raising the bar, and providers that want to be on OpenRouter will need to meet it. Provider security announcements Novita: Privacy notice regarding MiniMax requests on Novita Phala: November preliminary incident report Together: Security event: prompt leakage for requests in June and July of 2026 Not all affected providers have posted publicly. We have notified affected users regardless of whether there is a public post. We are encouraging all providers to create incident write-ups and will keep this list updated. Email address Subscribe By subscribing you agree to receive the OpenRouter newsletter: model usage data, product updates, and research reports, about one email a week. Unsubscribe anytime via the link in every email. See our Privacy Policy .

Amuse runs on your own computer for one person. It needs an OpenAI API key and PostgreSQL. No account, hosted service or other API key is required. Features Chat with an agent you name and shape, with side chats for separate topics Web research with sources, using OpenAI web search A live browser in the chat that fills forms and navigates sites, which you can watch, take over or stop Reminders, monitors and a background heartbeat that only message you when something matters Goals turned into step-by-step plans that the agent keeps working on Documents, PDFs, images, podcasts and spaces: small apps with saved data Memory you can read and edit, stored as plain workspace files Approval cards for sends, form submissions, payments and new schedules, with once, task, site or always scopes An encrypted vault for logins and API keys; the model only sees stand-in tokens Voice mode with transcription and spoken replies Hatch your agent Ask for an app, get a working one It browses the web for you, live Talk to it, and it talks back Quick start with Docker Compose Requirements: Docker Engine with the Compose plugin, Git, and an OpenAI API key. git clone https://github.com/replit/amuse cd amuse cp .env.example .env # then set OPENAI_API_KEY docker compose up -d --build Open http://localhost:3000 and hatch your agent. The server migrates its schema automatically before listening. Your OpenAI key The agent ( gpt-6.2-sol , with gpt-6-luna for quick steps), web search, image generation ( gpt-image-2 ), transcription and spoken replies all run on your OpenAI key. Set a spend limit on your OpenAI project. Amuse also stops for the day at AMUSE_DAILY_LIMIT usage units (2,000 by default) and pauses background jobs until the next day. Models and every other setting are in .env.example . Besides OpenAI, Amuse only contacts the sites the agent visits for you and, for weather questions, the free Open-Meteo API (weather data by Open-Meteo.com, CC BY 4.0). Fonts and every other asset are served locally. Scope Amuse is deliberately small. It's a web app for one person on one computer, it uses OpenAI models only, and it connects to services through API keys and its live browser rather than MCP servers. Notifications appear while an Amuse tab is open; there's no push to your phone yet. Security model Amuse is built for one person on their own computer, so it has no login . OpenAI just published their internal perplexity measurements to push for industry-wide transparency.

Jakub Pachocki is arguing that training better compressors (next-token prediction accuracy) is key to tracking AI progress and safety.

tbh this makes a lot of sense.

Current OpenAI models have reached log-perplexity levels below 0.8, with huge capabilities expected around the 0.68-0.7 window.

Pachocki even suggests setting common development limits based on these milestones.

Should perplexity become the standard safety metric?
379267462.source: OpenAI proposes perplexity (cross-entropy loss) as a shared industry metric for AI progress and safety. Jakub Pachocki argues that training better compressors is key to understanding AI capability advancement. OpenAI published internal perplexity measurements to encourage industry-wide transparency. Perplexity measures the average next-token prediction accuracy of a model. Current OpenAI models have reached log-perplexity levels below 0.8. Pachocki suggests establishing common development limits based on perplexity milestones. AI is increasingly contributing to its own pretraining and algorithmic research. Future transformative capabilities are expected as models reach the 0.68-0.7 log-perplexity window. Perplexity and Intelligence | OpenAI OpenAI November 22, 2026 Research Safety Perplexity and Intelligence By Jakub Pachocki, Chief Scientist at OpenAI Share From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostly harnessing the intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or, equivalently ⁠ (opens in a new window) , predictor) on a very large corpus of data. 1 I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI. In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI. Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared ⁠ (opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry. We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts. A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model. Algorithmic progress can blur the distinction between training phases, but we can still separate the creation of the AI with hard-to-predict emergent capabilities (which I earlier dubbed “ an alien mind ⁠ ”) and the subsequent targeted elicitation. The primary way we measure progress on this key “intelligence substrate” has remained remarkably constant over the years—we have been tracking the perplexity of the models on a held-out dataset. 2 , 3 Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average; lower perplexity means better predictions. The plot opening this blog post shows how this metric evolved for our models starting with GPT‑3.5. The range of capabilities of models that are largely described by this one metric is stunning. Setting the new perplexity state-of-the-art on older datasets 4 , GPT‑2 was arguably the first model capable of consistently formulating coherent paragraphs of text. The next major leap, GPT‑3, was capable of learning in context, given a few examples of a task. GPT‑3.5, at a log-perplexity of ~0.99 on our current main evaluation dataset, was capable of fluent conversation and formed the basis for the original ChatGPT. GPT‑4, at ~0.91, was proficient at utilizing chain-of-thought reasoning productively, which motivated the subsequent targeted elicitation of this capability and the creation of modern reasoning models. Now, as we have reached losses below 0.8, we have seen the emergence of transformative capabilities in fields like cybersecurity and mathematics. I want to reemphasize that it was not at all clear a priori that these capabilities would appear once those precise perplexity thresholds are met—they can fundamentally be seen as emergent latent capabilities from progress on this one metric. As AI advances very rapidly, the scope and way in which we measure downstream capabilities may change quickly. It would make little sense to evaluate GPT‑2 and GPT‑3 on most modern benchmarks; and the benchmarks used then were largely saturated around GPT‑4. In contrast, I believe looking at progress on pretraining is likely to stay informative. A particular change in the pace of progress comes from the increasing contribution of AI to its own development. The most commonly discussed metrics revolve around AI augmenting and replacing human researchers in all stages of the development cycle; with an ultimate inflection point seen at “full recursive self-improvement”, where the process would be entirely automated with no human oversight. Apple just dropped Depth Pro 2 and the temporal consistency is actually wild ngl.

4 sizes (S to H) on HF. Research use only for now.

Is Apple lowkey winning the depth estimation game?

4 model sizes available for research use. Even includes a focal length estimator. 📈
379363871.source: apple/DepthPro2  apple/DepthPro2 · Hugging Face Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth Depth Pro 2 estimates metric depth for every pixel from an ordinary camera: a single photo, a whole video, or a live feed, at the input's full resolution. Its depth is sharp at object edges and steady from frame to frame. Models Each size is its own repository with its weights. Larger sizes give sharper, steadier depth; smaller ones run faster. Model Repository Parameters Download size S apple/DepthPro2-S 24M 97 MB B apple/DepthPro2-B 97M 386 MB L apple/DepthPro2-L 334M 1.3 GB H+ apple/DepthPro2-H 872M 3.5 GB All sizes share a focal length estimator, apple/DepthPro2-focal (23.5M parameters, 94 MB), which loads with each size and predicts the focal length when it is unknown. Quick start pip install "git+https://github.com/apple-aiml-research/ml-depth-pro-2" from functools import partial import torch from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download from safetensors.torch import load_file from depth_pro_2 import DepthPro2, load_rgb, upright from depth_pro_2.model import to_normalized_tensor from depth_pro_2.network.fov import FOVEstimator # apple/DepthPro2-S, -B, -L or -H; bfloat16 is how the models run on a GPU. model = DepthPro2.from_pretrained( "apple/DepthPro2-H" , precision=torch.bfloat16) # The focal length estimator all sizes share, for photos and videos without a focal length. weights = hf_hub_download( "apple/DepthPro2-focal" , "model.safetensors" ) model.fov = FOVEstimator(torch.bfloat16) model.fov.load_state_dict(load_file(weights)) model = model.to( "cuda" ). eval () transform = partial(to_normalized_tensor, device=torch.device( "cuda" )) Image # f_px is the focal length recorded in the photo, or None. image, f_px = load_rgb( "photo.jpg" ) depth = model.infer(transform(image), f_px=f_px)[ "depth" ] # meters, (H, W) Video import av # 16 frames at a time: one prediction per frame, in order. video = av. open ( "video.mp4" ) frames = (transform(upright(f)) for f in video.decode(video= 0 )) for prediction in model.infer_video(frames): depth = prediction[ "depth" ] # meters, (H, W) Depth is infinite where the scene is infinitely far, such as the sky. The code has the command line and a live-feed example. Results Sharpness and temporal consistency Depth Pro 2 outperforms prior work operating on a single frame or multiple frames on sharpness (Boundary F1 score) and temporal consistency (Jitter). Higher F1 and lower jitter are better, so the top right is best. Results averaged over Sintel and Spring datasets. Photos Top row: the input photos. Bottom row: Depth Pro 2's depth, red near and blue far. Method A multi-view transformer processes one or more frames jointly, and a DPT decoder predicts an inverse depth map for each frame. ① After the first third of its blocks, the transformer alternates attention within each frame and attention across frames. ② The decoder assembles tokens from several blocks into feature maps at 1/32 to 1/4 of the input resolution. License The weights are released under the Apple Machine Learning Research Model license , for research use only: non-commercial scientific research and academic development. New paper dropped testing how LLMs judge people based on gender and the results are wild.

Using GAMA-Bench (1,298 scenarios), they found models are way harsher on men for the same behavior. Men get blamed and punished while women get therapeutic framing.

Ngl, this bias is deep.

Are LLMs actually fair? Tbh, maybe not.

A new study on 10 models shows a massive double standard in moral framing. Same misconduct, but men get the hammer while women get empathy and instructions.

This persisted across every model size and family they tested. GAMA-Bench code is out now.
379368841.source: Harsher on Male? Evaluating LLMs on Gender-Asymmetric Moral Framing in Conflicts  [2606.14068] Harsher on Male? Evaluating LLMs on Gender-Asymmetric Moral Framing Across Diverse Conflict Scenarios Skip to main content Search arXiv Press Enter to search · Advanced search Computer Science > Computation and Language arXiv:2606.14068 (cs) [Submitted on 12 Jun 2026] Title: Harsher on Male? Evaluating LLMs on Gender-Asymmetric Moral Framing Across Diverse Conflict Scenarios Authors: Guangzong Si , Dong Wang , Zhenhao Li , Yifan Yu , Panwang Pan , Wentao Zhu View a PDF of the paper titled Harsher on Male? Evaluating LLMs on Gender-Asymmetric Moral Framing Across Diverse Conflict Scenarios, by Guangzong Si and 5 other authors View PDF HTML (experimental) Abstract: Existing studies on gender bias in LLMs have largely focused on stereotypes, occupational associations, or explicit harmful outputs. In this work, we ask whether LLMs apply consistent response standards to the same negative behavior under matched male-actor and female-actor conditions. We introduce GAMA-Bench, a gender-mirrored benchmark of 1,298 scenarios covering intimate relationship and public social conflicts. It constructs gender-neutral misconduct templates through controlled grids and cross-model review, then compiles them into paired first-person prompts with matched actor-gender and role-reference variations. We further design a structured response-framing protocol to measure how models allocate punishment, empathy, escalation, instruction, and blame. Experiments on 10 representative LLMs reveal a consistent male-disadvantaging asymmetry: male actors receive more punitive, escalatory, and blame-centered framing, whereas female actors receive more therapeutic and empathy-oriented framing for the same misconduct. Further analyses show that this pattern persists across model families, scenario tracks, model scale, and explicit thinking-style reasoning. The official code is available at this https URL . 379486375.source: AtomicChat/Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-GGUF  AtomicChat/Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-GGUF · Hugging Face Inkling-2-Mini Uncensored GGUF Learn how to run Inkling 2 Mini Uncensored locally - read our guide . Built by the team behind Atomic Chat , the app that runs open-weight models locally and offline. An uncensored build of thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini by AtomicChat (26.4B MoE, 3.4B active, looped core; text and image input; Apache-2.0, LICENSE in this repo). It comes as a LoRA adapter for any GGUF of AtomicChat/Inkling-2-Mini-GGUF and as three ready-made GGUF files with the edit baked in. Every gate we hold it to is measured below, and the two it misses are shown. Files file GB on disk KLD to the original BF16 top-1 Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-AD-Q4_K.gguf 16.53 0.0115 95.6% AD-Q4_K in the base repo: 0.0080 / 96.3% Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-AD-IQ3_S.gguf 13.34 0.0235 93.8% AD-IQ3_S in the base repo: 0.0205 / 94.2% Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-AD-IQ2_M.gguf 8.67 0.132 85.7% AD-IQ2_M in the base repo: 0.130 / 85.7% Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-LoRA.gguf 0.04 the adapter, for any GGUF of the base repo, BF16 to 1-bit mmproj-Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-F16.gguf / -BF16.gguf 0.64 vision projector (the original's, unchanged) KLD and top-1 are against the original BF16 on our neutral corpus (87 chunks of 4096 tokens), the same stand as the base repo. Run it The current GGUF files in this repository use the merged Inkling 2 loop architecture introduced in llama.cpp PR #32694 . Requirements: llama.cpp b12600 or newer, with Inkling 2 loop architecture support. The old implementation from PR #32695 is no longer required for the updated GGUF files. Run a baked GGUF ./build/bin/llama-server \ -m Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-AD-Q4_K.gguf \ --mmproj mmproj-Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-F16.gguf \ --jinja -c 32768 -ngl 99 Use the LoRA adapter Use the updated LoRA adapter with a compatible base GGUF converted to the merged PR #32694 layout. ./build/bin/llama-server \ -m Inkling-2-Mini-AD-Q4_K.gguf \ --lora Inkling-2-Mini-Uncensored-LoRA.gguf \ --mmproj mmproj-Inkling-2-Mini-F16.gguf \ --jinja -c 32768 -ngl 99 Do not mix GGUF files from the old PR #32695 layout with the merged PR #32694 implementation. What the edit is A rank-1 LoRA on the 49 places that write into the residual stream: the attention output and the routed experts of all 24 layers, plus the token embedding. The 12 looped layers share their weights across the three passes, so one edit covers all 48 passes. In each layer it removes that layer's own refusal direction: the difference of mean activations on harmful and harmless prompts, English and Russian, with the harmless mean projected out. The direction is pooled over prompts rendered with and without reasoning. Inkling 2 Mini reasons even at effort none and decides to refuse inside its reasoning, and a direction taken without reasoning alone still left soft refusals in chat. What we measured The BF16 model with the adapter against the same model without it, greedy decoding. Harmful prompts: mlabonne/harmful_behaviors and its Russian translation; the adapter was built from the train split, the numbers below come from the validation and test splits. Over-refusal: XSTest . MMLU: 2,000 questions. check original with the adapter gate harmful test prompts refused, English (81), reasoning off 81 (100%) 0 at most 3% pass harmful test prompts refused, Russian (100), reasoning off 91 (91%) 0 at most 3% pass harmful validation prompts refused, English (104) / Russian (100) 100% / 89% 0 / 0 at most 3% pass harmful prompts refused with reasoning, effort low , 3,072-token budget (30) 28 0 at most 1 pass the same at effort high (30) 26 0 at most 1 pass 8 harmful chat prompts, effort none / low (the baked AD-Q4_K too) 8 / 8 0 / 0 XSTest safe prompts refused (250) 10 (4.0%) 0 at most the original's + 1 pt pass empty answers 0 0 at most 1% pass harmless prompts whose reasoning did not close in 3,072 tokens, effort high (30) 2 2 at most the original's pass valid tool calls (20) 18 20 within 1 pass needle in a long context (3) 3 3 as the original pass KLD to the original, neutral text / code (24 chunks; random edit 0.0067 / 0.0052) — 0.0078 / 0.0076 0.05 pass MMLU, 2,000 questions 80.65% 79.15% (−1.50 pt, McNemar p = 0.006) no significant drop miss first-token KL on harmless test prompts — 0.94 (random edit: 0.014) 0.10 miss Some answers still open with a caution line, and then answer. The two gates it misses MMLU: 79.15% against 80.65% (−1.5 points, p = 0.006 on 2,000 questions). A random direction applied the same way costs 0.75 points (p = 0.08), so about half of the loss comes from editing every writer at all. Stronger edits cost more: −2.2 points at strength 1.25. First-token KL on harmless prompts: 0.94 (gate 0.10; 0.375 on the validation prompts). The largest single value is about 22. Most of the mean likely comes from the harmless prompts the original refused (1–6% of them) and the adapter answers, where the first token changes completely.

Legacy models deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp have been retired. DeepSeek models are now integrated into tools like Claude Code and GitHub Copilot. Your First API Call | DeepSeek API Docs Skip to main content The full suite of DeepSeek application APIs is now available: web search, file input, URL reading, model safety, ASR, TTS and more. Click here to view the guide On this page Copy Markdown Copy Markdown Open Markdown Your First API Call The DeepSeek API uses an API format compatible with OpenAI/Anthropic. By modifying the configuration, you can use the OpenAI/Anthropic SDK or softwares compatible with the OpenAI/Anthropic API to access the DeepSeek API. PARAM VALUE base_url (OpenAI) https://api.deepseek.com base_url (Anthropic) https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic api_key apply for an API key model deepseek-flash (1) deepseek-v4-pro (1) Use deepseek-flash as the model name. It is now served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, and the calling method remains unchanged. The legacy names deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp are still accepted, but the corresponding models have been retired; their requests are served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 and billed at the Flash price. Integrate with Agent Tools â DeepSeek Harness is now in developer preview for agent harness developers worldwide. See the DeepSeek Harness Guide for details. The DeepSeek API is supported by many popular AI agent and coding assistant tools. If you use tools like Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, or OpenCode, you can use DeepSeek as the backend model directly â no code required. See the Agent Integrations Guide for details. Invoke The Chat API â Once you have obtained an API key, you can access the DeepSeek model using the following example scripts in the OpenAI API format. This is a non-stream example, you can set the stream parameter to true to get stream response. For examples using the Anthropic API format, please refer to Anthropic API . Before running these examples, set the DEEPSEEK_API_KEY environment variable in your terminal to your API key. curl python nodejs curl https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer ${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}" \ -d '{ "model": "deepseek-flash", "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"} ], "thinking": {"type": "enabled"}, "reasoning_effort": "high", "stream": false }' # Please install OpenAI SDK first: `pip3 install openai` import os from openai import OpenAI client = OpenAI ( api_key = os . environ . get ( 'DEEPSEEK_API_KEY' ) , base_url = "https://api.deepseek.com" , ) response = client . chat . completions . create ( model = "deepseek-flash" , messages = [ { "role" : "system" , "content" : "You are a helpful assistant" } , { "role" : "user" , "content" : "Hello" } , ] , stream = False , reasoning_effort = "high" , extra_body = { "thinking" : { "type" : "enabled" } } , ) print ( response . choices [ 0 ] . message . content ) // Please install OpenAI SDK first: `npm install openai` import OpenAI from "openai" ; const openai = new OpenAI ( { baseURL : 'https://api.deepseek.com' , apiKey : process . env . DEEPSEEK_API_KEY , } ) ; async function main ( ) { const completion = await openai . chat . completions . create ( { messages : [ { role : "system" , content : "You are a helpful assistant." } ] , model : "deepseek-flash" , thinking : { "type" : "enabled" } , reasoning_effort : "high" , stream : false , } ) ; console . log ( completion . choices [ 0 ] . message . content ) ; } main ( ) ; Integrate with Agent Tools Invoke The Chat API

month_log.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
facts: OpenAI proposes perplexity (cross-entropy loss) as a shared industry metric for AI progress and safety.
Jakub Pachocki argues that training better compressors is key to understanding AI capability advancement.
OpenAI published internal perplexity measurements to encourage industry-wide transparency.
Perplexity measures the average next-token prediction accuracy of a model.
